_about: Budgets are ratios against a yardstick measured in the same run and beside the layer it divides -- dictionary, integer and string work in a loop, never this project's code -- because seconds recorded on one machine cannot gate another, and a yardstick written in C would barely notice which interpreter called it while this project is Python all the way down. The yardstick is measured again in every pass, next to the layer, because measuring it once at the start cancels steady load out and amplifies load that lands on one window and not the other: at the old sequence, bursts timed onto the yardstick alone drove the reported ratio to 0.41x and onto the layers alone to 1.33x, on one idle machine with one unchanged tree, and a loaded machine turned an unchanged tree red twice in twenty-four runs. Passes continue past the first three while they disagree by more than a quarter, because under load the fastest of three can still be a pass where only one of the two numbers got a clean window. One entry per operating system, because the ratio does not travel between them either; a platform with no entry passes and says so, since there is no way to write a budget for a machine before a run on it -- but `platforms_expected` lists the keys that already have one, because a platform loses its budget by being renamed as easily as by being deleted and both look like silence. Adding a platform means adding it in both places, which is the point: one of them is the claim and the other is the figure. The seconds below are for a reader and are also compared: a layer whose absolute time collapses has stopped doing its work, which no ratio can tell from a fast machine.

Darwin._from: one run on an idle machine, chosen as the closest to the mean of five. Re-recorded when `supplied_template` joined the layers and when deciding which submodels a table answers for stopped being recomputed once per rule -- the second of those is why `corpus_pass` fell from 111 to 97.5, and leaving the old figure would have been a budget with twelve percent of slack nobody could account for. Those five spanned cold_start 56.4-62.1 (10% peak to peak), corpus_pass 97.5-101 (4%), scale 79.7-86.0 (8%), rules_layer 0.417-0.451 (8%), supplied_template 27.4-29.7 (8%). Peak-to-peak over a stated number of runs is the figure worth quoting; a standard deviation of three samples reads reassuringly and hides what a reader meets. The yardstick itself came out about half the seconds it did when these were first recorded, on the same machine, which is what the ratios exist to absorb and did. Under heavy background load an unchanged tree has been measured between 0.54x and 1.74x, so the warning line at 1.5x is inside the noise on a loaded machine and is advisory, while the failure line at 2.0x has not been crossed by an unchanged tree since the yardstick moved beside the layer. Re-recorded again for `corpus_pass` alone when the corpus gained four inputs judged with a table supplied on the command line (61 to 65), and only that layer: nothing in the package moved -- the change is in `tools/` -- and re-recording the other four would have thrown away the drift they exist to show. Fifteen runs, and they do not support a precise figure: 93.4 to 110, 18% peak to peak, against the 4% the five above spanned. Spacing them 45 seconds apart did not narrow it, so it is another process on the machine rather than heat, and the mean and the median agree at 104, which is the figure; the seconds beside it come from the run that measured it. What the four inputs cost is inside that dispersion and this does not claim otherwise -- the same tree read 101 and 102 with 61 inputs earlier in the same hour, against a budget of 97.5, so most of the move is the machine and not the corpus. A reading within a tenth of this budget is therefore not evidence of anything; the thresholds below are what the gate decides on, and the layer that actually regressed was measured at 3.98x. Taking the memoisation back out puts `supplied_template` at 3.98x, measured. Re-recorded, all five layers, when the File-reference work and the record of what a run did not open were merged: the corpus grew from 65 inputs to 67 (two File-reference cases on a Nameplate) and the package changed under every layer. Five runs spanned cold_start 58.8-61.1 (4% peak to peak), corpus_pass 102-106 (4%), scale 80.5-86.6 (8%), rules_layer 0.437-0.474 (8%), supplied_template 28.5-29.8 (5%), and the run kept is the one closest to their mean. Against the figures they replace every layer moved by less than the dispersion recorded above for an unchanged tree, so what this says is that the merge cost nothing measurable -- not that it cost nothing. Re-recorded for `corpus_pass` alone when the corpus gained the case `scopeNotExamined` was built for (67 inputs to 68): the change is in `tools/`, and the other four are left as they were so they go on showing their drift. Five runs spanned 103-109 (6% peak to peak), and the one closest to their mean is kept. Re-recorded, all five layers, when IDTA 02011 landed: a seventh pack registers eleven rules under every layer, the walk now gives a nested copy the rows of the element it copies and records what it reached, and the corpus gained the vendored 02011 template and two Hierarchical Structures cases (68 inputs to 71). Five runs spanned cold_start 59.4-64.7 (9% peak to peak), corpus_pass 107-111 (4%), scale 83.8-87.9 (5%), rules_layer 0.482-0.496 (3%), supplied_template 29.7-30.8 (4%), and the run kept is the one closest to their mean. Against the figures they replace, scale rose by 6% and rules_layer by 10% -- the second outside the dispersion recorded for an unchanged tree. That layer times one table's analysis of the 02004 example and never reaches the new pack, so the eleven rules are not the reason: timing the parent's engine and this one side by side in one process on that workload gave 1.04 to 1.05, the cost of the walk that now carries copies and records what it reached, and the rest of the ten percent is the machine -- these five runs were made with other work on it, the yardstick reading about 1.4 times its last record's, so they are not the idle runs the first sentence of this entry describes. corpus_pass rose by 4% over three more inputs and the other two layers moved within noise. Re-recorded, all five layers, when IDTA 02007 landed: an eighth pack registers seventy-three rules under every layer, and the corpus gained the vendored 02007 template and two Software Nameplate cases (71 inputs to 74). Five runs spanned cold_start 58.1-61.5 (6% peak to peak), corpus_pass 107-118 (10%), scale 84.8-89.0 (5%), rules_layer 0.465-0.493 (6%), supplied_template 28.4-30.8 (8%), and the run kept is the one closest to their mean; no other heavy process was on the machine when they started. Against the figures they replace, corpus_pass rose by 2% over three more inputs and the other four fell by 1 to 4%, every move inside the dispersion recorded above for an unchanged tree: the seventy-three rules cost nothing this measures, which is not the same as costing nothing. Re-recorded, all five layers, when IDTA 02035-5 landed: a ninth pack registers fifty rules under every layer, and the corpus gained the vendored 02035-5 template and two Product Condition cases (74 inputs to 77). Five runs spanned cold_start 55.9-60.5 (8% peak to peak), corpus_pass 108-127 (18%), scale 69.5-73.1 (5%), rules_layer 0.461-0.491 (7%), supplied_template 30.0-31.1 (4%), and the run kept is the one closest to their mean. Against the figures they replace, scale fell by 15% in all five runs -- outside the dispersion recorded above for an unchanged tree -- and nothing in this change reaches the pass it times, three thousand elements no row describes and none near one; the figure is kept as measured, which tightens that budget and explains nothing. corpus_pass rose by 3% over three more inputs, well inside the 18% these five spread over, and the other three layers moved by 3% or less. The yardstick read about a quarter to a third slower than at the last record on rules_layer and supplied_template, so these runs were not on the idle machine the first sentence of this entry describes; the ratios are what absorbs that.
